what: Just above a section header, a strip of square cells in 4 rows is laid, and while the section header rises from the bottom of the screen to the top, cells switch on one by one so the section color crumbles down like stairs — cell order is (row weight × .38 + random × .72) / 1.1, so rows farther from the section light up later. Cells are 28px at 1440 width (17px below 700), and if vertical guides are given, columns are cut at each line so the lines and cell edges interlock. With edge: bottom, the strip below the section tail starts fully on and switches off toward the document end

options.edge: top (above the section head, default) · bottom (below the section tail, retracts to the document end)
options.guides: CSS selector for the vertical baseline that splits the columns (e.g. .rules__line). If none, the chosen cell
options.keep: Baseline selector where lines break but no line is drawn at cell borders, default [data-rule-keep]
options.rules: on: Draws a faint vertical line in the baseline-position cell
options.seed: Random order seed (to vary when a page has several bands), default 0
options.tail: Reveal length when bottom (ratio of remaining scroll), default .8
options.--fx-tile: Cell color — sets the background color variable of the sheet that covers it (style="--fx-tile: var(--kf-contrast-bg)")

note: The band is attached outside the section (bottom:100%) so it overlaps the previous section. The original also changes the header text color (brightness .5 threshold) and baseline mask over the band area, but that is the site’s job

from.where: .pxt in index.html·technology.html — at every spot where the black and white sections switch (original Base script pixel transition: 28/17px cells · 4 rows · .38/.72 weight · threshold .02+.98 · tail band before footer .8)
